name: Lifshitz Spacetime
description: A spacetime whose symmetry rescales time and space by different powers, $t \to \lambda^z t$ while $x \to \lambda x$, written down by Shamit Kachru, Xiao Liu, and Michael Mulligan in 2008 as the gravitational dual of a Lifshitz critical point. At $z = 1$ it is anti-de Sitter space, and for $z > 1$ every curvature scalar is constant while the tidal forces diverge on a null singularity at $r = 0$.
convention: The dynamical exponent $z \ge 1$ is a pure number and $L$ is a length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Zoom out from a system at its critical point and it looks the same as before, provided the film of it is slowed down to match [kachru2008]. By how much? For a relativistic theory the answer is by the same factor, $t \to \lambda t$ when $x \to \lambda x$, and anti-de Sitter space is the spacetime of one more dimension that has that rescaling for a symmetry [kachru2008]. Critical points in magnets and liquid crystals can answer with a power, $t \to \lambda^z t$, where the dynamical exponent $z$ is not 1 [kachru2008]. The model case has $z = 2$: a scalar field whose action pairs $(\partial_t\phi)^2$ with $(\nabla^2\phi)^2$, the theory of what R. M. Hornreich, Marshall Luban, and S. Shtrikman named in 1975 "a multicritical point of a new type, hereafter called a Lifshitz point" [kachru2008, hornreich1975].¶The spacetime that does for such a point what anti-de Sitter space does for a conformal one came in August 2008 from Shamit Kachru, Xiao Liu, and Michael Mulligan [kachru2008]. They asked for a metric that keeps its form under the lopsided rescaling, with the scale itself a new radial coordinate that goes as $r \to r/\lambda$, and for translations, rotations, and reflections of space and time besides [kachru2008]. The answer takes one line, $ds^2 = L^2(-r^{2z}dt^2 + r^2d\mathbf{x}^2 + dr^2/r^2)$: anti-de Sitter space in its Poincaré chart with the clocks at each depth retuned by a power of $r$, and anti-de Sitter space itself at $z = 1$ [kachru2008]. Only $g_{tt}$ holds $z$, so every moment of it is the same hyperbolic space, whatever the exponent [kachru2008]. The same pair of warp factors had turned up in December 2007, in five dimensions, when Peter Koroteev and Maxim Libanov filled the space beside Randall and Sundrum's wall with an anisotropic fluid [koroteev2008, copsey2011].¶A negative cosmological constant by itself makes anti-de Sitter space, so what holds the clocks out of tune? Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan used two gauge fields in four dimensions, joined by a topological coupling, and found that real fields require $z \ge 1$: the dual theories may show "critical slowing down" and never "critical speeding up" [kachru2008]. That December Marika Taylor did the same work with a single massive vector field, and the two models are dual to one another [taylor2008, copsey2011]. The black holes that put the dual theory at a temperature came the same month from Ulf Danielsson and Lárus Thorlacius, a family in which the area fixes the charge, and in 2011 Thorlacius, Ville Keränen, and Esko Keski-Vakkuri formed one from a shell falling in at the speed of light [danielsson2009, keranen2012]. String theory supplied the $z = 2$ spacetime in 2010, when Koushik Balasubramanian and K. Narayan, and Aristomenis Donos and Jerome Gauntlett, rolled up an anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions along the null direction of a wave crossing it [balasubramanian2010, donos2010].¶Fall toward $r = 0$ and the tidal forces grow without bound while every curvature scalar stays what it was [kachru2008, copsey2011]. Each scalar built from the Riemann tensor is a constant, the Ricci scalar $-2(z^2 + 2z + 3)/L^2$, yet the spacetime is geodesically incomplete, and Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan warned that "an infalling object experiences very large tidal forces" there [kachru2008]. The numbers are Keith Copsey and Robert Mann's, from 2010: in the falling frame the forces grow as $r^{-2z}$ for every $z$ but 1, the surface $r = 0$ is null, and its past half is in view of every observer, a naked singularity [copsey2011]. Their diagram of the whole is the Poincaré patch of anti-de Sitter space with singularities where its horizons would be [copsey2011]. Gary Horowitz and Benson Way sent a string in and found it "infinitely excited" on the way through [horowitz2012lifshitz]. At Stanford in 2012 Ning Bao, Xi Dong, Sarah Harrison, and Eva Silverstein had the matter that holds the spacetime up slow the string first, and Harrison, Kachru, and Huajia Wang had corrections to the dilaton models swap the deep interior for $AdS_2 \times R^2$ [bao2012, harrison2014].¶The boundary needed mending as well: Penrose's rescaling, which brings the infinity of anti-de Sitter space in to a finite place, leaves a degenerate metric on the boundary here, since time and space blow up at different rates [keeler2014]. The repair, Petr Hořava and Charles Melby-Thompson's anisotropic conformal infinity of 2009, rescales the two by different powers, and with it Lifshitz spacetime has a boundary of the usual dimension, carrying $-dt^2 + d\mathbf{x}^2$ up to the same lopsided rescalings [horava2011]. Light feels the imbalance too: its coordinate speed along $\mathbf{x}$ grows as $r^{z-1}$, without bound toward the boundary [keeler2014].¶So how much of the interior can the boundary see? Follow the light rays, as Cynthia Keeler, Gino Knodel, and James Liu did in 2013: one aimed straight at the boundary arrives, and one with any momentum along $\mathbf{x}$ turns around short of it and falls back [keeler2014]. They proved the quantum version as well, that local data on the boundary cannot rebuild the local fields inside, for Lifshitz spacetime or for any flow that passes through a Lifshitz region [keeler2014]. In her review of 2016 Taylor counted the dictionary between fields inside and operators on the boundary as "still not completely understood" for Lifshitz theories [taylor2016].

related.text: Lifshitz spacetime at $z = 1$, where time and space scale alike. There the edge $r = 0$ is the horizon of the Poincaré chart, with more spacetime beyond it [kachru2008, copsey2011].
A wave of Siklos's form crossing anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions, rolled up along the wave's null direction, is Lifshitz spacetime at $z = 2$ [balasubramanian2010, donos2010].
Near $r = 0$ Lifshitz spacetime looks like a singular plane wave, which is how Horowitz and Way sent strings through its singularity [horowitz2012lifshitz].

Randall and Sundrum's wall warps time and space by one factor. Koroteev and Libanov gave the two different factors by filling the space beside it with an anisotropic fluid, and met Lifshitz's scaling in five dimensions [koroteev2008].
The same scaling of time against space with Galilean boosts and a conserved mass besides, which takes one more dimension, a null one [son2008, balasubramanian2008].

coordinates.name: Kachru-Liu-Mulligan
domains: r \to 0 \;\text{(a null singularity of the tidal forces for } z > 1\text{)}

parameters.description: Dynamical exponent: under $t \to \lambda^z t$, $x \to \lambda x$, $y \to \lambda y$, and $r \to r/\lambda$ the metric keeps its form (a pure number, $z \ge 1$; $z = 1$ is anti-de Sitter space)
Curvature radius (a length); the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -(z^2 + z + 4)/2L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, x, y, r)$ of Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$, $y$, and $r$ lengths. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Inverse Radius
domains: u \to \infty \;\text{(a null singularity of the tidal forces for } z > 1\text{)}

parameters.description: Dynamical exponent: under $t \to \lambda^z t$, $x \to \lambda x$, $y \to \lambda y$, and $r \to r/\lambda$ the metric keeps its form (a pure number, $z \ge 1$; $z = 1$ is anti-de Sitter space)
Curvature radius (a length); the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -(z^2 + z + 4)/2L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, u)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$, $y$, and $u = L^2/r$ lengths, where $r$ is the radius of Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Proper Distance
domains: \rho \to -\infty \;\text{(a null singularity of the tidal forces for } z > 1\text{)}

parameters.description: Dynamical exponent: under $t \to \lambda^z t$, $x \to \lambda x$, $y \to \lambda y$, and $r \to r/\lambda$ the metric keeps its form (a pure number, $z \ge 1$; $z = 1$ is anti-de Sitter space)
Curvature radius (a length); the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -(z^2 + z + 4)/2L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, \rho)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $x$ and $y$ lengths, and $\rho = L\ln(r/L)$ the proper distance along the radius $r$ of Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Tortoise
domains: w \to \infty \;\text{(a null singularity of the tidal forces for } z > 1\text{)}

parameters.description: Dynamical exponent: under $t \to \lambda^z t$, $x \to \lambda x$, $y \to \lambda y$, and $r \to r/\lambda$ the metric keeps its form (a pure number, $z \ge 1$; $z = 1$ is anti-de Sitter space)
Curvature radius (a length); the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -(z^2 + z + 4)/2L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, w)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $x$ and $y$ lengths, and $w = L^{z+1}/(zr^z)$ the tortoise coordinate of the radius $r$ of Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan, a length. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein
domains: r \to 0 \;\text{(a null singularity of the tidal forces for } z > 1\text{)}

parameters.description: Dynamical exponent: under $t \to \lambda^z t$, $x \to \lambda x$, $y \to \lambda y$, and $r \to r/\lambda$ the metric keeps its form (a pure number, $z \ge 1$; $z = 1$ is anti-de Sitter space)
Curvature radius (a length); the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -(z^2 + z + 4)/2L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, x, y, r)$, all lengths, with $r$ the radius of Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan and $v = ct - L^{z+1}/(zr^z)$ the advanced time, constant along each ingoing light ray of fixed $x$ and $y$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Affine Null (Copsey-Mann)
domains: s \to 0 \;\text{(a null singularity of the tidal forces for } z > 1\text{)}

parameters.description: Dynamical exponent: under $t \to \lambda^z t$, $x \to \lambda x$, $y \to \lambda y$, and $r \to r/\lambda$ the metric keeps its form (a pure number, $z \ge 1$; $z = 1$ is anti-de Sitter space)
Curvature radius (a length); the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -(z^2 + z + 4)/2L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(v, x, y, s)$ of Copsey and Mann, all lengths, with $v = ct - L^{z+1}/(zr^z)$ the advanced time and $s = (2L/z)(r/L)^z$ an affine parameter along each ingoing light ray of fixed $x$ and $y$, where $r$ is the radius of Kachru, Liu, and Mulligan. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
